question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (AMD)

calls.reasoning: AMD guided Q3 2026 revenue to $13.0B ±$0.3B (Aug 4, 2026); consensus ~$13.06B. Over the last 8 quarters AMD beat its guidance midpoint every time, by +1.8% to +7.0% (median ~+4%; Q1'26 +4.6%, Q2'26 +3.0% vs $11.2B guide). Applying the typical beat gives a median near $13.45B. Data center and Helios/MI450 demand reportedly tracking ahead of forecast supports upside; Gaming decline and supply constraints cap it. Market check: no human market on AMD revenue found (Polymarket/Manifold none; Kalshi only mention markets). Escapes outside $12.0-14.2B need a >7% miss or >9% beat, unprecedented in the sample, so no escape mass is declared.

calls.reasoning: AMD guided Q3 FY2026 revenue to $13.0B ±$0.3B on Aug 4, 2026, and consensus is about $13.06-13.1B. AMD has beaten its guidance midpoint in all 8 of the last 8 quarters, by +1.8% to +7.0%. The last four beats were +6.3%, +7.0%, +4.6% and +3.0%, so a beat of about 3.5% is a reasonable centre, giving a median near $13.45B. Strong data center demand (Helios/MI450, server revenue growing more than 80% YoY) gives a right skew. A big Gaming decline and tight supply of wafers, packaging and HBM limit how large the beat can be. Landing above $14.2B would take a beat of more than 9%, which has not happened in the sample, so that is priced at about 2%. No mechanism exists for a result below $12.0B. Market check: none of the three runs found a revenue-level market on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi, only mention markets and an earnings-beat market, none of which match this contract. No new search was possible on this run.
calls.reconciliation: The three runs agree on every fact: the guide is $13.0B ±$0.3B, consensus is about $13.06-13.1B, the report comes Nov 3, the revenue history matches the question, and no market or pre-announcement was found. Their beat histories are consistent; Run 1's is the most complete (8 quarters, +1.8% to +7.0%). The only disagreements are judgments. (1) How big the beat will be: medians range from about 3% (Run 2) to about 4% (Runs 1 and 3). The latest beat was the smallest of the recent ones (+3.0%), but the four-quarter median is about 5%. I take about 3.5%, which gives $13.45B; the dossier evidence puts me there, not an average of the runs. (2) Upper escape mass: I agree with Run 3 that the chance is small but not zero, given AI upside, and price it at 2%. I carry Run 1's dispersion forward, slightly widened.
